name: Mbabane
subtitle: Mbabane, capital of Eswatini: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

keyPoints.text: Mbabane was conferred city status in 1992, which created the Mbabane City Council.
When King Mswati III took the throne in 1986, Mbabane was still largely an administrative town; population grew from about 38,290 (1986) to 60,691 (2017).

parts.text: Mbabane was conferred city status in 1992, which created the Mbabane City Council.
When King Mswati III took the throne in 1986, Mbabane was still largely an administrative town; population grew from about 38,290 (1986) to 60,691 (2017).
Mbabane's history is traced to Chief Mbabane Kunene, who settled the area in the 1750s (the likely origin of the name; the tourism page does not explicitly say the town was named for him).
The British moved the administrative capital of Swaziland from Manzini to Mbabane after the Boer War damaged Manzini.
The Manzini municipal council records that after the Anglo-Boer war ended in May 1902, British settlers preferred the highveld for the administrative capital.

items.text: Chief Mbabane Kunene settles in the area.
After the Anglo-Boer war the British make Mbabane the colonial administrative capital (sources give 1902 or 1903).
Independence; Mbabane begins to expand markedly.
Mbabane has about 38,290 residents and is still largely an administrative town.
City status conferred; Mbabane City Council created.
Corporate Place introduces high-rise commercial development.
Limkokwing University of Creative Technology is established in the city.
